title: Yugoslav Wars
summary: The wars that broke up Yugoslavia began after Slovenia and Croatia declared independence on 25 June 1991. The war in Bosnia and Herzegovina was the deadliest: more than 100,000 people were killed and two million forced to flee. In 1995 Serb forces executed more than 8,000 Bosnian Muslim men and boys at Srebrenica, an act of genocide. Fighting followed in Kosovo in 1998–1999 and in Macedonia in 2001.

uncertainty.note: Began with the Ten-Day War in Slovenia and Croatian fighting in June 1991; major fighting ended with the Dayton Accords in 1995, followed by Kosovo in 1998–1999 and the Ohrid settlement in 2001.
